summary: Back to full health and playing like the best tight end in the league through Raiders camp, per multiple beat reports — no lingering issue from 2025. Confirms last year's elite per-game rate is a reliable 2026 baseline.

Not the starter (Bowers is), but Kubiak's heavy 12/13-personnel scheme means Mayer projects to play the first snap of most games in a two-TE set — a real receiving/blocking role, not a token backup, behind an elite TE1.

Sophomore breakout candidate after a Pro Bowl rookie year (817 yards, franchise record); reported to be "quietly elite" through camp, with a thin Colts WR room opening the door to an even larger 2026 target share than his already-high rookie usage.

Missed offseason workouts recovering from groin surgery (Week 17 2025 injury) but was a full camp participant from Day 1 with no setback; his 107 rookie targets should grow further in Year 2 under new QB Deshaun Watson.

Re-signed on a 1yr/$7M deal; role could expand further in 2026 after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown to New England, opening up target share in an already-productive 2025 (career-high 11 TDs). Limited in camp by a calf injury, not considered serious.

Opened camp on PUP (first team reps in nine months) but returned to 11-on-11 and caught all five targets, looking fully healthy; GM Brian Gutekunst says he hopes to get a contract extension done before Week 1, still unresolved as of mid-August.

Playing "like crazy" through camp per Andy Reid, who says coaches have had to pull the oldest player on the roster out of reps to manage his workload — no sign of an age-related decline yet, despite "last dance" retirement speculation from his own camp for 2026.

Left Cleveland (his only team for 9 years) in free agency for a one-year, up-to-$8M deal with the Chargers. His prior Browns target share/scheme context is irrelevant to a 2026 projection; he's now working with first-team reps in LA's TE room alongside Charlie Kolar.

Being phased out of the Chargers' 2026 offense: after a productive rookie year (49-664-3 on 69 targets), he's been running with the fourth-string QB in camp while free-agent addition Charlie Kolar and new signee David Njoku work with the 1s. His rookie per-game rate is a poor baseline for a 2026 role that's shrinking, not growing.

Signed a 3-year, $53M extension that resolved persistent offseason trade speculation (multiple teams had reportedly called about him); enters 2026 secure as Atlanta's primary receiving TE after a breakout second half of 2025.

Signed a contract extension and remains the Patriots' only returning TE with real snaps; New England released 2025 receiving leader Stefon Diggs (who signed with Washington) and instead added Romeo Doubs, leaving Henry positioned as Drake Maye's top target again.

Remains atop the Saints' TE depth chart after a career-high 2025 (77-889-3), but the team added Noah Fant in free agency and drafted Oscar Delp in round 3 specifically to expand two-TE sets — his target monopoly is less complete than last year's numbers suggest.
Signed with New Orleans in free agency to push the Saints toward more two-TE sets; expected to make the 53-man roster behind Juwan Johnson but his target share is unproven in this offense.

A camp injury scare (limped off during 11-on-11) turned out to be incidental, not a knee issue. More importantly, he enters 2026 fully healthy after missing 9 games combined over his prior two seasons — durability, not talent, has been the swing factor in his per-game output, and this camp is a clean bill of health so far.

Tore his ACL in Week 14 of the 2025 season, ending that year early. Plans to play a 14th NFL season and is expected to be cleared around Week 1, but Washington has made no official commitment to him for 2026 as of camp — his roster spot itself is unresolved, not just his health.
Positioned to move into the Commanders' starting TE role for 2026 with Zach Ertz's status uncertain coming off a torn ACL — a clear opportunity increase from a committee role in 2025.

Had two offseason surgeries immediately after Seattle's Super Bowl LX win but says he's fully recovered and expects to build on a breakout 2025 (52-519-6, TE1 in all three playoff games). Second-round rookie Elijah Arroyo is a name to watch for target-share creep, but Barner remains the clear TE1 entering 2026.
Signed a new extension and enters camp fully healthy as Houston's unquestioned top TE after a career-high 2025 (82-777-3) — a stable, low-uncertainty situation relative to most of this list.

2nd-round rookie (Michigan) has repeatedly flashed in the passing game through camp, rotating with the 1s and scoring in practice multiple times; coach DeMeco Ryans called his camp "very encouraging." A real path to the TE2 role as a rookie behind Dalton Schultz.
Signed a 3-year, $30M extension and enters 2026 as Tampa Bay's unquestioned TE1, with the new offensive scheme reportedly increasing TE usage in the passing game beyond his already-heavy 2025 role.

Signed a 3-year, $39.3M extension that resolves offseason cut/trade speculation and locks him in as Baltimore's TE1 — but has had a rough start to camp with multiple drops, worth monitoring since it's an early, small-sample concern rather than a role change.

Left Baltimore in free agency for a $40M deal with the Giants and was placed ahead of incumbent Theo Johnson on New York's first unofficial depth chart — a full team-context change from his Ravens role that last year's stats don't reflect.

Listed behind free-agent signee Isaiah Likely on the Giants' first unofficial depth chart despite being heavily involved with rookie QB Jaxson Dart in OTAs — still very much in the offense, but no longer the presumptive lead TE his 2025 role implied.

Signed a 3-year, $36M extension and enters 2026 fully healthy after missing 5 games in 2025; new OC Liam Coen has him working an expanded, multi-alignment role in camp — a clear opportunity increase from an already-productive (540 yards in 12 games) 2025.

Operating as the Jets' top TE in camp while 1st-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq recovers from a hernia (see separate note), but has himself had a rocky camp with dropped passes — his role is secure short-term, his efficiency is a real early question.

The Jets' first-round rookie TE has been sidelined since the first week of August with a hernia issue, delaying what was expected to be an immediate two-TE role alongside Mason Taylor. No timeline given as of mid-August.

Steelers cut TE-room competitor Jonnu Smith (see separate note) and let Connor Heyward leave in free agency, clearing snaps for Freiermuth; new OC Brian Angelichio previously coached tight ends in Minnesota and is expected to feature the position more than 2025's crowded rotation did.

Released by Pittsburgh in early March after a down 2025 (38-222-2, a big drop from his Miami production) and signed a one-year deal with Green Bay. His current-roster listing may still show Pittsburgh in some feeds — this is a confirmed, completed team change, not a rumor.

No new knee concerns reported in 2026 camp — connected with the QB for three touchdowns in a single 7-on-7 period on Aug. 17. His prior ACL/MCL injury (Dec. 2023) is now two full offseasons behind him with no setback signs.

Emerging as San Francisco's de facto TE1 with George Kittle beginning camp on PUP recovering from his Achilles (see separate Kittle note); signed a 2-year, $8M deal and has drawn touchdowns from Brock Purdy in red-zone drills. If Kittle's return lingers into the season, Tonges opens with real workload.

The Rams' TE room (Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, rookie Max Klare) is being treated as a true four-way committee by the coaching staff, with OC Nate Scheelhaase saying he doesn't expect any one player to emerge — none of last season's individual usage numbers for these four should be assumed to carry forward unchanged in 13-personnel-heavy sets.

Spent much of the 2026 offseason undecided on whether to keep playing before signing with Carolina in mid-August — well after most teams' camps opened. He's being eased in gradually (sat out joint practices and a preseason game), so a full Week 1 workload is not assured despite the signing.

Healthy through camp (touchdown catch on Day 1) entering his second season with Denver; new playcaller Davis Webb was Engram's draft classmate and the team traded for WR Jaylen Waddle, both of which project positively for a passing offense that used him for only 50-461-1 in his debut Broncos year.

Named a breakout candidate for 2026 after a franchise-record rookie season for a TE (44-357, 16 games). Entering Year 2 as a core piece of new playcaller Brian Daboll's retooled offense (see the Titans' broader offensive-overhaul note on Cam Ward).

Locked into a run-blocking/two-way role in Ben Johnson's three-TE system (with Colston Loveland and rookie Sam Roush) rather than a receiving-focused one — he took a backseat in the passing game in 2025 (30-347-2) once Loveland arrived, and nothing in camp suggests that changes in 2026 even though he remains a key on-field piece.

Re-signed on a 3-year, $25.5M deal and remains Cincinnati's primary receiving TE (Drew Sample handles run-blocking duty), healthy through camp and looking to return to his 2024 form (65-665-0-ish receiving level).

Left practice early with an ankle injury described as "bad news" for Carolina's TE room; awaiting further testing as of the report. A real availability risk during a camp the team has otherwise called injury-plagued.

2nd-round rookie has had an unremarkable camp and is buried behind Dallas Goedert and Johnny Mundt on the depth chart; beat writers expect him to open 2026 on the bench with a real role unlikely unless there's an injury ahead of him.
